tools.name: count_leads
tools.description: How many leads match an ICP, and what pulling them would cost at this account's prices. Free: this call never spends credits. It is the only way to size an audience without paying per row, which makes it the first step before search_leads. A realtime count is not free ($0.04 flat at the Tier 0 list price); it runs only when mode:"realtime" is passed explicitly.

job_titles.description: Target job titles, OR-matched (e.g. ["CEO","Founder","Owner"]). A lead needs to match only one.

seniorities.description: Seniority at the current employer, e.g. ["Owner","CXO","VP","Director","Manager"]. Current position only.

locations.description: Where the lead lives — matches cities, states and countries, e.g. ["United States","Berlin"].

company_locations.description: HQ location of the lead's current employer.

company_industries.description: Industry of the current employer. Must match Generect industry names exactly (e.g. "Software Development", "Financial Services"); names are hierarchical and unknown names are rejected with HTTP 400 naming the field.

company_types.description: Employer types: "Public Company","Privately Held","Non Profit","Government Agency","Educational","Self Employed","Self Owned","Partnership".

company_name.description: Anchor to one company by name (exclusive with company_link/company_id).

company_link.description: Anchor to one company by LinkedIn URL.

company_id.description: Anchor to one company by LinkedIn numeric id.

exclude_names.description: Skip leads by full name. Works in both modes (the database-mode bug that returned 0 rows was fixed in the API on 2026-08-13, PRO-1333). exclude_ids is still the more reliable way to paginate.

exclude_ids.description: Skip leads by Generect/Sales-Navigator id. Pass the ids you already received to paginate without duplicates — ordering is not stable, so this is more reliable than offset.

filter_empty_vars.description: Drop leads where these fields are empty, e.g. ["profile_photo","job_started_on"]. Useful to raise data quality before paying.

allow_unlisted_values.description: Escape hatch. This server checks industry / seniority / headcount / company-type values against the LinkedIn vocabularies before sending, because the API silently returns 0 results for an unknown industry or seniority instead of rejecting it. Set true only when you are sure a value is valid and this server is out of date.

tools.name: get_balance
tools.description: Account balance, month-to-date usage and this account's own per-operation prices. Free: this call never spends credits. balance_usd is the wallet; grants_usd is bonus and plan credit (sign-up bonus, perks, plan allowance), reported apart. Grants are spent first, but only on the operations each one covers: a promo perk or a plan allowance may not pay for API calls, and a perk never pays for phone numbers, so the two figures do not add up to what the account can spend. Useful before a batch of paid work (what the user can afford) and after it (what was spent). These are the account's real rates; prices in tool descriptions are list prices.

include_transactions.description: Also return the N most recent transactions (each shows the operation type and dollar amount).

include_prices.description: Include this account's per-operation prices. Default true.

include_usage.description: Also return the month-to-date credit usage broken down by operation type. Free.

include_token_analytics.description: Also return per-API-token request counts for the last 30 days (by endpoint and status). Free. Useful for answering "which integration is making these calls?".

tools.name: health
tools.description: Liveness check. Free: this call never spends credits. Confirms the MCP server is up, reports its version and (unless disabled) verifies the credential against a free account endpoint. It never touches a paid data endpoint, so it is safe for monitors.

check_credential.description: Also verify the API token against the free /accounts/me endpoint. Default true.

tools.name: preview_leads
tools.description: A cheap look at the actual people behind a count, before a full search. Billable: about $0.002 per returned row at the Tier 0 list price. Accounts can pay a different rate: get_balance returns this account's prices, and every response reports what was actually spent in cost.amount_charged_usd. Preview rows carry a Generect `id`, so the usual flow is: preview many, pick the few that fit, then enrich_lead or generate_email only on those. By the API contract preview rows are masked (no LinkedIn URL, domain, email or phone); an account that gets more than that cannot rely on it.

confirm_spend_usd.description: Explicit approval for an unusually large charge. Calls whose worst case exceeds $5 are refused unless this is set to at least the amount the tool reports. Only set it after the user has agreed to that number.

tools.name: resolve_profile
tools.description: Reveal who is behind an anonymous LinkedIn profile link. Billable: about $0.0005 per resolved profile (an unresolvable reference is free; duplicates in one batch are billed per row) at the Tier 0 list price. Accounts can pay a different rate: get_balance returns this account's prices, and every response reports what was actually spent in cost.amount_charged_usd. Takes the obfuscated links that Sales Navigator leaves in exports, CRMs and ad platforms (`linkedin.com/in/ACwAA…`), plus Sales Navigator lead URLs, bare profile ids and urns, and returns the real profile URL and identity. `profiles` (up to 50) resolves a batch in one call. The `id` it returns is the identifier enrich_lead, generate_email and find_phone accept, so this is the cheap first step before a full record. Returns identity only (no location, company or work history; enrich_lead has those). The numeric member id is not accepted as input (LinkedIn answers 403 to it); it comes back as `linkedin_id`.

url.description: A single LinkedIn person reference: profile URL of any flavour (including /in/ACwAA… and /sales/lead/…), a public identifier, an obfuscated id (ACwAA… or ACoAA…) or an urn. Matched case-insensitively.

id.description: Alias for `url` — same accepted values. Use whichever reads better.

profiles.description: Batch mode: 1–50 references, mixed freely. One row per input, in input order, each either a resolved profile or {input, error}. Duplicates are billed per row — deduplicate first.

compact.description: Default true: return a small per-profile summary (including the Generect `id`, which every later step accepts). Set false for the full raw record (~80 fields) — only worth it when you specifically need skills, education or other deep fields.

tools.name: enrich_lead
tools.description: Full profile for one known person, by Generect id, LinkedIn URL or work email (reverse lookup). Billable: about $0.02 per record found (not-found is refunded) at the Tier 0 list price. Accounts can pay a different rate: get_balance returns this account's prices, and every response reports what was actually spent in cost.amount_charged_usd. Not found costs nothing. The `id` from a search or preview result is the most accurate identifier. start_bulk_job handles many people at once.

mode.description: Data mode. "database" = Generect's own index: sub-second, free counts, free thin rows (see detail) or cheaper full rows; it accepts a subset of the filters today and names any it rejects. "realtime" = live LinkedIn lookup, 5–60s, billed per row, accepts every realtime filter. "auto" (default) tries database first and escalates to realtime only if a filter you passed is rejected there (the escalation is reported, and is refused above the per-call spend ceiling). Pick "database" explicitly when a record from the last 12 months is good enough and cost matters more than freshness.

tools.name: generate_email
tools.description: Find and verify a work email. Billable: about $0.02 per VALID email found (a miss is free) at the Tier 0 list price. Accounts can pay a different rate: get_balance returns this account's prices, and every response reports what was actually spent in cost.amount_charged_usd. Identifies the person by lead_id (most accurate), LinkedIn URL or first name, last name and domain. `candidates` resolves several people in one call; more than 10 go to an async bulk job instead, which returns a job_id for get_bulk_job.

lead_id.description: Generect lead id from search / preview / enrich results — the cheapest and most accurate identifier.

domain.description: Company domain without protocol, e.g. "stripe.com" (name+domain mode).

candidates.description: Batch mode. Each entry uses the same identifier rules as the single-person form.

tools.name: validate_email
tools.description: Check deliverability of emails you already have. Billable: about $0.005 per email submitted (every address is billed, whatever the verdict) at the Tier 0 list price. Accounts can pay a different rate: get_balance returns this account's prices, and every response reports what was actually spent in cost.amount_charged_usd. This is the one operation where every submitted address is billed: the verdict is the deliverable. An address generate_email returned as valid is already verified, so validating it again only adds cost.

emails.description: Email addresses to validate. Each one is billed.

tools.name: find_phone
tools.description: Find a phone number for one person. Billable: about $0.4 per phone found (a miss is free) at the Tier 0 list price. Accounts can pay a different rate: get_balance returns this account's prices, and every response reports what was actually spent in cost.amount_charged_usd. The most expensive operation here, roughly 20x an email lookup, so it suits people the user has already qualified rather than a whole list. start_bulk_job takes an approved list.

lead_id.description: Generect lead id from search / preview / enrich results — the cheapest and most accurate identifier.

domain.description: Company domain without protocol, e.g. "stripe.com" (name+domain mode).

tools.name: start_bulk_job
tools.description: Submit up to 50 records for asynchronous processing and get a job_id back. Billable at the same per-record rate as the single-record tool, and the whole cost is reserved at submit time: a submitted job keeps running (and charging) even if nobody polls it. Meant for a list the user has approved. get_bulk_job polls it, and a webhook (create_webhook) reports when it finishes.

job_type.description: What to do with the items. phone_find is by far the most expensive per record.

mode.description: Enrich jobs only: cached (cheaper) or live. Default "database".

confirm_spend_usd.description: Explicit approval for an unusually large charge. Calls whose worst case exceeds $5 are refused unless this is set to at least the amount the tool reports. Only set it after the user has agreed to that number.

tools.name: get_bulk_job
tools.description: Status and results of a bulk job. Free: this call never spends credits. Polling is free (the work was billed at submit time); a few seconds between polls is enough.

tools.name: list_webhooks
tools.description: List the webhook endpoints registered for bulk-job completion events. Free: this call never spends credits.

tools.name: create_webhook
tools.description: Register a URL that receives bulk-job completion events, so scheduled or unattended workflows are notified instead of polling. Each event carries the job's results (emails, phone numbers or records) in its body. Free: this call never spends credits.

url.description: URL that receives the events, http or https. The API refuses a host that resolves to a private or internal address.

secret.description: Shared secret for HMAC signature verification.

tools.name: update_webhook
tools.description: Change the URL, events or signing secret of a registered webhook. Free: this call never spends credits. A new URL changes where completion events, and the results they carry, are delivered; a new event list changes which events are sent.

url.description: New URL for the events, http or https. The API refuses a host that resolves to a private or internal address.

events.description: New list of events, at least one.

secret.description: New shared secret for HMAC signature verification.

tools.name: delete_webhook
tools.description: Delete a registered webhook; its endpoint stops receiving completion events. Free: this call never spends credits.

tools.name: test_webhook
tools.description: Send a test event to a registered webhook endpoint. Free: this call never spends credits.
